metadata.title: A Thermodynamically-Grounded Sub-Threshold p-Bit Coprocessor for RISC-V: Physical FPGA Realization, Stochastic Universality, and Industrial Energy Benchmarks
metadata.description: As classical microelectronics scaling approaches the Boltzmann thermodynamic limit (~60 mV/decade at 300 K), thermodynamic and probabilistic computing offer a transformative alternative for non-deterministic workloads. This dataset and preprint package introduces the design, mathematical formalization, Verilog RTL implementation, and physical silicon proof of a 32-bit RISC-V (RV32I) core coupled with a thermodynamic Probabilistic Processing Unit (PPU) and Native Hybrid ALU. Built upon coupled p-bits governed by the continuous Langevin equation and an RTL Piecewise Linear (PWL) Boltzmann activation engine, this work overcomes the fundamental non-linear separability of stochastic logic gates using an autonomous hidden-unit topology (H = A AND B). Implemented and verified on physical Gowin GW1NR-9C FPGA hardware (Sipeed Tang Nano 9K) at 27 MHz (Fmax = 87.84 MHz), the core demonstrates full compliance on the NIST SP 800-22 cryptographic entropy suite (Runs Test P-value = 0.28902), exact Ising Hamiltonian ground-state convergence, and 100% deterministic decision accuracy under 500-cycle continuous pipeline stress (BER = 0.00e+00). At the Swanson-Meindl sub-threshold limit (70 mV), dynamic power dissipation is reduced by 99.51% (204.1x per cycle), delivering task-level energy savings of up to 25,510x in inverse integer factorization and 16,326x in combinatorial optimization over conventional 1.0 V RISC-V processors. Includes complete IEEE-format manuscript, vector benchmark figures, and an open-access educational Verilog RTL package distributed under the Thermodynamic Hardware Fair-Source License (TH-FL-1.0).
